findings.title: Migration crashes when the optional legacy category setting is unset
findings.body: The join returns no rows when `embed_category` has its normal blank/default value, has no persisted row, or names a category that no longer exists. Indexing `[0]['id']` then raises before the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` can run, preventing `db:migrate` on those installations. Read the first result defensively and apply the uncategorized fallback when no matching category exists.

findings.title: Legacy URL-form host settings are migrated into values that can never match
findings.body: This raw INSERT bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callbacks. Existing settings such as `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/path` are stored verbatim, but `record_for_host` parses a request down to `eviltrout.com` and queries `lower(host) = ?`; it therefore cannot find these migrated rows. The previous setting implementation explicitly supported schemes and paths, so affected sites will lose embedding authorization after upgrading. Normalize each legacy value before inserting it (and preferably use the model or bound SQL).

findings.title: Duplicate host records make the destination category ambiguous
findings.body: There is no case-insensitive uniqueness validation or database constraint on `host`, while lookup selects an unordered `.first` matching row. The admin API permits adding the same host more than once with different categories, after which new embeds can be assigned to whichever duplicate the database happens to return rather than the category the administrator intended. Enforce normalized, case-insensitive host uniqueness with a database index as well as model validation.

findings.title: Hosts entered with a port are accepted but cannot be authorized
findings.body: The validation explicitly permits a port and the normalization callback retains it (for example, `example.com:8080`), but `URI(host).host` removes the port before this query. The stored value `example.com:8080` is consequently compared with `example.com` and never matches, so configured non-default-port embedding sites are always rejected. Normalize ports out of persisted host values or consistently compare host and port.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid modern domain names
findings.body: The hostname expression limits the final label to two through five ASCII letters. Valid domains such as `example.museum`, `example.technology`, and other long modern TLDs cannot be added through the new admin UI and receive a validation error, even though they are valid embedding origins. Use URI/domain parsing or a TLD-length-independent hostname validation.

findings.title: Updating or deleting a missing host returns a 500
findings.body: Both `update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first` without handling a nil result. A stale edit after another administrator deletes the host, or a request for an unknown id, calls `save_host(nil)` or `nil.destroy` and raises `NoMethodError` instead of returning a not-found response. Explicitly fetch-or-404 before saving or destroying.

findings.title: The data migration is not reversible despite using `change`
findings.body: The migration performs several raw `execute` calls inside `change`; Rails cannot infer inverses for them, so `db:rollback` raises an irreversible-migration error. Even if the table were removed, the deleted `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site-setting values have no restoration path. This blocks rollback deployments and permanently discards the prior configuration; implement explicit `up` and `down` paths that restore the old settings.
